front: How is a bond payable initially measured, and how is interest expense computed under the effective interest method?
back: Initial carrying amount = PV of cash flows at the market rate at issuance. Interest expense = beginning carrying amount x market rate at issuance; amortization = interest expense - coupon paid.

front: Carrying amount and interest expense over time: discount versus premium bond
back: Discount bond: interest expense > coupon, carrying amount and interest expense rise toward face value. Premium bond: interest expense < coupon, carrying amount and interest expense fall toward face value.

front: Gain or loss on early debt redemption
back: Gain (loss) = carrying amount - amount paid to redeem. Paying less than carrying amount gives a gain; paying more gives a loss. Reported in the income statement.

front: Cash flow statement classification of bond cash flows
back: Issue proceeds and principal repayment: financing. Coupon payments: operating under US GAAP; operating or financing under IFRS.

Single model: record a lease liability (PV of lease payments) and a right-of-use asset. Expense = depreciation of the ROU asset + interest on the liability, so total expense is front-loaded. Exemptions: short-term (12 months or less) and low-value leases.

front: US GAAP lessee: finance lease versus operating lease
back: Both put an ROU asset and lease liability on the balance sheet. Finance lease: depreciation + interest (front-loaded). Operating lease: a single straight-line lease expense, with the whole payment in operating cash flow.

Grant-date fair value (options valued with an option pricing model, adjusted for expected forfeitures) is expensed, usually straight-line, over the vesting period, with an offsetting increase in contributed capital.

front: Treasury stock: what is it and how does it affect equity?
back: Own shares repurchased and held. It is a contra-equity account that reduces total equity and shares outstanding. No gain or loss goes through the income statement on reissue.

front: Effect of cash dividend, stock dividend and stock split on total equity
back: Cash dividend: reduces equity. Stock dividend: transfers retained earnings to contributed capital, total equity unchanged. Stock split: no change in equity, more shares and a lower par value per share.

front: What does accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) contain?
back: Unrealized items that bypass net income: foreign currency translation adjustments, unrealized gains and losses on certain investments (FVOCI), cash flow hedge gains and losses, and pension remeasurements.

front: Interest coverage and fixed charge coverage formulas
back: Interest coverage = EBIT / interest payments. Fixed charge coverage = (EBIT + lease payments) / (interest payments + lease payments).
